text:
maya: Quick sync — we need to decide whether to surface a "BatchHint" and a predictive-window control in the scheduler API. Problem: microbursts cause us to either wait too long (latency spikes) or flush tiny batches (cost/kernel overhead).

kevin: Agree. Main tradeoff is 99th latency vs throughput. Any hint API must not let tenants starve the shared fastpath.

olivia: Suggestion: use a short EWMA of inter-arrival for each tenant + a sliding deadline. If arrival-rate predicts another token in 10-30ms, hold; otherwise cut. That keeps microburst packing without long waits.

sam: To make this practical, exposing a small opt-in hint could work. Example config idea:
```
batch_hint:
  deadline_ms: 30   # soft target
  policy: predictive
  granularity: tenant
```

lia-bot: deploy-stats: ci-batcher 03/24: after enabling 25ms window in canary, p95 stable, p99 +18% during peak. :warning: 

maya: Important: we also need a clear fallback for single-request SLOs. If request has tight deadline header, bypass predictive hold.

kevin: Thinking about scheduling signals: instead of special headers, we could have a "batch_credit" token that the control plane mints for high-priority requests. Scheduler treats credited requests as preemptive. Simpler admission: credits > 0 => immediate enqueue to fastpath.

olivia: Credits help but can be gamed. Need quota enforcement and decay. Also KV-cache eviction: holding requests longer increases KV reuse and reduces model compute but reduces freshness for streaming contexts. We should add a freshness flag on hints.

sam: Freshness flag + deadline makes sense. Quick sketch of request metadata:
```
{
  "deadline_ms": 50,
  "batch_hint": "predictive",
  "freshness": "stale_ok"
}
```

maya: Starvation mitigation idea: reserve a tiny percentage of slots (soft-reserve lane) for sub-50ms requests. If reserved lane empty, refill to prevent unused capacity.

kevin: And telemetry — we must instrument enqueue time, batch formation time, and effective kv-hit-by-rule. Without that we won't know if predictive wins.

olivia: I'll prototype an admission shim that computes EWMA and toggles a hold flag per-tenant. Will include metrics and an opt-in header.

maya: Great. Action items: olivia prototype + perf dashboard, kevin to draft credit/quota sketch, sam to write API shape and SLO bypass rules. We'll reconvene after a 2-week prototype run.

lia-bot: reminder: created ticket INF-9821 for the prototype (owner: olivia).
